subject: Next steps: qualification + structured actions / function-calling requirements
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@clearbank.com>, Tom Harper <t.harper@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:02:00-05:00
Subject: Next steps: qualification + structured actions / function-calling requirements

Thanks again for the 45-minute intro today — appreciated the practical examples, Elena. Quick recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned on pain, goals, and the concrete qualification items we discussed.

Pain points you called out
- Legacy rules engine adds 150-250ms call latency when enriching transactions; overall authorization path sometimes hits 400ms tail latency.
- Batch reconciliation jobs are expensive and brittle; inconsistent embeddings across vendors means mismatch in customer search.
- Need deterministic, auditable outputs for automated remediation workflows.

Current stack you shared
- Ingest & routing: Kafka -> internal microservices
- Models: on-prem transformer ensemble for embeddings (Finlytics-managed) + PostgreSQL for metadata
- Orchestration: Airflow + home-grown webhook dispatcher for operational actions

Success criteria (what will make a pilot successful)
1) Sub-200ms 95th percentile for synchronous enrich call in the authorization path (for 1–2k reqs/min).
2) Deterministic JSON-formatted action payloads (strict schema, no free-text) that can be consumed by your webhook dispatcher.
3) >30% reduction in per-token inference cost in the reconciliation workload via batching/caching/quantization.

Conclusions / proposed qualification checklist (items you asked us to confirm)
- Function-calling / structured outputs: Redwood will produce schema-validated JSON action objects; we’ll provide a sample schema and an automated handshake (schema negotiation + validation error handling). (See attached proposed-map.json for initial schema draft.)
- Determinism: we’ll pin generation configs, temperature=0 for production paths, and add output hashes for traceability.
- Integration: we can deploy a small sandbox in your EU region and expose a test webhook endpoint for end-to-end validation. Link below.
- Compliance: we will share SOC2 artifact pointers and outline encryption-in-transit+at-rest behavior.

Next steps (action owners / timeline)
- Redwood: share a minimal JSON schema + sample function contract and a sandbox deployment by end of day Friday. (Owner: Markus)
- ClearBank: share the small set of remediation actions you expect (3–5 actions) and your webhook contract (headers, auth) by EOD Thursday. (Owner: Elena)
- Tech sync: 30-minute sandbox walk-through (engineering-to-engineering) next Tuesday 10:00 AM GMT. (Tentative — please confirm availability)

Attachments: redwood-high-level-arch.png, proposed-map.json

Best,
Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0189

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@clearbank.com>

Cc: Tom Harper <t.harper@finlytics.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: qualification + structured actions / function-calling requirements

Thanks Markus — clear and helpful. Two clarifications from our side: 

1) On determinism: the remediation payloads must be byte-for-byte stable for the same inputs for auditability. We will supply a canonical test vector set (10 examples). Can Redwood produce a stable SHA256 digest over the serialized JSON we can compare on ingest?

2) Security: for the sandbox we need mutual TLS and a short-lived client cert approach. Can you confirm mTLS support for the sandbox endpoint?

3) Attachments: saw the proposed-map.json — Tom and I will add two more action definitions and return a single combined JSON by Thursday.

Also, can you include a short note on how Redwood handles partial failures in a function-call chain (e.g., if an enrichment tool is unavailable, what does fallback look like)? That will determine how we map the webhook retry semantics.

Happy to run the Tuesday slot if it stays at 10:00 AM GMT.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Product Risk & Automation, ClearBank
elena.rossi@clearbank.com

Elena / Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround on items. Final confirmation and a couple logistics notes before the sync: 

- Deterministic digest: yes — we will add a digest header (X-Redwood-Output-Digest) in the webhook response. The CLI that Dev is building will compute the canonical serialization and SHA256.
- mTLS sandbox: confirmed — the sandbox supports mTLS with short-lived cert issuance via our test CA; we’ll provision a client cert for you prior to the tech sync.
- Partial failures: default behavior in the pipeline is "fail-open" for low-risk enrichment (we return a minimal recovery object and log a trace) and "fail-closed" for actions that would modify state (we return 409 + retry_hint). We’ll include the full flow in the sandbox README.

Scheduling: we’ve booked the 30-minute slot on Tuesday 2026-11-17 10:00–10:30 GMT and created a sandbox instance (https://redwood.app/sandbox/rdw-8392). I shared a Drive folder with the proposed-map.json and a short README describing the validation harness.

Action items recap
- Redwood (Markus): sandbox + client cert + sample outputs + README (by Mon COB).
- ClearBank (Elena): canonical test vector set (10 examples) + finalized action definitions (by Thu EOD).
- Redwood (Grace/Dev): pricing sketch and CLI/digest tool (internal deliverable by Mon).

If that all looks good, I’ll send the calendar invite and a short pre-read.

Best,
Markus
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
